title: Prenatal exposure to organophosphate pesticides and neurobehavioral development of neonates: a birth cohort study in Shenyang, China.
ehr_evidence: A cohort of the mothers and their neonates participated in the study and information on each subject was obtained by questionnaire; urine samples were collected for dialkyl phosphate (DAP) metabolite analysis.
summary: A birth cohort study of 249 healthy pregnant women and their neonates in Shenyang, China (2011-2012) examining the association between prenatal organophosphate pesticide exposure (urinary DAP metabolites) and neonatal neurobehavioral development (NBNA scores).
key_findings: Prenatal total DAP concentrations were inversely associated with NBNA scores; a 10-fold increase in DAP concentration was associated with a decrease of 1.78 in NBNA Summary scores (95% CI, -2.12 to -1.45).
There was a 2.11-point difference in summary NBNA scores between neonates in the highest quintile of prenatal OP exposure versus the lowest quintile group.
Significantly negative correlations between summary NBNA scores and maternal DMs, DEs, and DAPs (r = -0.510, r = -0.494, r = -0.561, P<0.01).
Higher prenatal DAP concentrations were associated with lower scores in all NBNA scales, especially the Behavior Scale (β for a 10-fold increase = -0.65, 95% CI, -0.85 to -0.45, P<0.01).
Prenatal OP exposure was the strongest risk factor for lower NBNA scores (largest standardized regression coefficients, P<0.05).

For female neonates, maternal urinary DAP concentrations were associated with poorer summary NBNA scores (β = -2.03, P = 0.01); for male neonates, a 10-fold increase was associated with a 1.47-point decrease.
High umbilical cord blood lead concentration and prenatal BMI were associated with poor NBNA scores (P<0.05); maternal age, education, and neonatal bodyweight had no significant associations.
captured_features: maternal age, education, gestational age, prenatal BMI, passive smoking
urinary DAP metabolite concentrations (DMP, DMTP, DEP, DETP, DEDTP) adjusted for creatinine
NBNA scores (Behavior, Passive Tone, Active Tone, Primary Reflexes, Summary)
pathologies_diseases: impaired neonatal neurobehavioral/neurodevelopmental outcomes (lower NBNA scores)
population: 249 healthy pregnant women and their neonates recruited from obstetric wards at the Central Hospital Affiliated to Shenyang Medical College, Shenyang, China (February 2011 to August 2012)
exposure_domain: organophosphate pesticide exposure (urinary dialkyl phosphate metabolites)
limitations: OP urinary metabolites were measured at a single time point prior to delivery, and DAPs have a short half-life (<24 h), so concentrations reflect only recent exposure with high variability.
Urinary DAP concentrations cannot quantify exposure to a particular pesticide.
Selection bias from enrolling only healthy pregnant women and excluding neonates with neurodevelopmental disorders; response rate 81.1%.
